completed: Audited venue_availability/venue_reservations RLS policies and grants across the active chain and confirmed the leak by direct read of the two source migrations: 20250814123000_venue_core.sql:302 creates "Anyone can view venue availability" FOR SELECT USING (true), and 20260823140000_reservation_conflict_engine.sql:81 creates venue_reservations_public_read FOR SELECT USING (true) with REVOKE on venue_availability only from anon/PUBLIC (lines 287-288) and no REVOKE at all on venue_reservations.

Audited every app/lib caller of both raw tables: a tree-wide scan for .from("venue_availability") / .from("venue_reservations") across app/, lib/, components/ now returns exactly one file, lib/venue/availability.ts, which imports "server-only" and is reached only after a canManageVenue gate. The previous client-role reader, app/venue/hooks/use-venue-calendar-data.ts, no longer imports @/lib/supabase/client at all.

Authorized additive migration 20260924120000: REVOKE SELECT from anon, public, authenticated on both raw tables; GRANT SELECT to service_role; drop the two permissive client SELECT policies; create venue_availability_service_read and venue_reservations_service_read TO service_role; leave venue_reservations_operator and the availability owner FOR ALL policies untouched; document on both tables that raw rows are service-role/venue-scoped only.

Made the migration fully re-runnable for a CP-051 operator retry: each new CREATE POLICY is now preceded by DROP POLICY IF EXISTS on its own name, so a partial apply converges instead of raising a duplicate-policy error. Recorded the reasoning in the migration header and the manifest's idempotency field.

Documented why the REVOKE does not break the public projection: public_venue_availability is WITH (security_barrier = true) and NOT security_invoker, so PostgreSQL resolves its access to venue_availability as the view owner, not the calling role. The contract test asserts the view grant and a resolvable query as a guard against a future security_invoker change.

Added executable runtime denial probes to the hosted contract test: for both raw tables and both anon and authenticated, SET ROLE then a count(*) ... where false must raise insufficient_privilege. A successful read raises a contract violation; any other error (missing role, missing table) raises a distinct 'probe inconclusive' error. A pg_has_role precondition refuses to run unless the runner is a MEMBER of both roles, with an explicit 'do not report this as a pass' message, so a misconfigured runner can never be mistaken for a passing boundary.

Added __tests__/venue/venue-availability-scope-migration.test.ts (12 invariants): client SELECT revoked on both tables, service_role SELECT retained, both permissive policies dropped, both new policies created TO service_role USING (true), no statement anywhere grants select to a client role or alters default privileges, write policies and RLS enablement never dropped, the sanitized view never revoked or dropped, each new policy dropped by its own name before creation, the contract test still carries the catalog and runtime probes, and the manifest digest matches the migration bytes with all three environment evidence slots null.
